hypothesis: Wave-5 task from the rpc-baseline record's reported-only candidate 1: 'get_available_models on the RPC surface pays ~773.9ms per call BECAUSE it WRITES models.json every call (the registry cache persist - a durable write on a READ command)'. TS-parity-first, then baseline-decompose the write path at the current tip (when/where models.json is written per call, the write's size, the trigger, who reads it back), then the candidate per the parity finding, then paired ABBA on the RPC surface with the fresh-write class labeled.
approach: PHASE 1 TS-PARITY: TS get_available_models (daemon-mode.ts:5125-5129 and in-process-agent-connection.ts:172) = await session.modelRegistry.refreshAvailableModels() on the SESSION'S LONG-LIVED registry; TS NEVER writes models.json (read-only user config; grep of the TS model-registry/auth paths: only reads + loadCustomModels). TS's refresh-chain disk writes are write-on-FETCH-SUCCESS only: PI live catalog writeCache(cachePath, payload) every successful fetch (prime-inference-model-catalog.ts:203-207; coalesced per cachePath via pendingRefreshes; offline short-circuit), private-authorization writePrivatePrimeAuthorizationCache only on a fingerprint-changing fetch success or a stale-TTL background refresh success (model-registry.ts:1052,1093), provider-catalog CatalogCache refresh('public',{force:false}) hour-gated (model-catalog-cache.ts). PHASE 2 RUST DECOMPOSE at origin/rust 5395ce47d (worktree lane/perf-rpc-models-persist, VM t86iotff0jv0u63uhp4ra0x8 hillclimb-perf-rpc-models-persist ubuntu:22.04 16c/32GB/100GB, rustup 1.98.1, cargo build --release --locked --workspace rc=0, binary sha 8ab45e64cf72dd04af24daa10b1a000d0e3f97e3e88f4a9755aee1a62f67d649, 222770104 bytes): the RPC surface handler is rpc/model_commands.rs:165 get_available_models -> registry(state) (FRESH registry per call) + registry.refresh_available_models().await - the FULL TS-parity awaited chain; the DAEMON worker surface (state_getters.rs:311 handle_get_available_models -> worker_model_registry) and the ACP surface (acp/config_options.rs discover_available_models) are the port's instant no-refresh handlers (an internal divergence between the port's own surfaces). Census+audit+component-probe legs (rpc_probe_gam.py: per-trial fresh agent dir/home/tmp/cwd, scrubbed env + venv-env.json, loadavg quiet gate, product-only zombie sweep, 10ms nonblocking frame pump, per-gam-call file audit of the 4 models-cache-class files + full agent-dir census, response raw-byte capture; gam_probe.rs VM-only component bin; strace -ff -f -tt -T -yy census; probe_v09 I/O preflights per block). PHASE 3 CANDIDATE + ABBA: A-B-B-A interleave 2 rounds x 4 blocks, binary staging unlink-then-copy with sha asserts pre/post per block, io-probe before every block.
parity_notes: The persist-on-read premise is REFUTED (three-level evidence): (1) CODE: the only writers of models-cache-class files are write-on-fetch-success paths - store_snapshot (pa-models/src/cache.rs:387 via write_atomic, provider-model-catalog.v1.json + prime-inference-models-cache.json) and write_private_prime_authorization_cache (pa-core/src/models/private_auth.rs:164, prime-inference-private-models.json); models.json itself is NEVER written by any product path (tests only). The port is ALREADY convergence option (a) persist-on-refresh-only, with the SAME contract as TS: write-on-success + CatalogCache CATALOG_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS hour-gate (state carried by the process-shared catalog_for OnceLock map, matching TS's long-lived-registry gating) + 5-min PRIVATE_PRIME_AUTHORIZATION_CACHE_TTL_MS. (2) PER-CALL AUDITS: 141 steady-state get_available_models calls across 5 decompose trials -> ZERO file changes. (3) CENSUS (strace -yy, path-accurate): no write-flag opens on models.json-class paths in any steady gam window. The baseline record's 773.9ms p50 (n=16) was an artifact of the battery design: one gam per trial x 16 fresh processes = every measured call was a PROCESS-FIRST call paying the awaited refresh chain; the write the baseline census caught in one gam window (open_wronly+rename+fsync, substring-matched 'prime-inference-private-models.json' as 'models.json') was the process-first call's own store_snapshot persist landing inside its own window - once per process, not per call. THE REAL GAP the decompose exposed: the RPC surface fires NO boot-time registry refresh - TS session boot resolves the initial model through refreshAvailableModels (model-resolver.ts:543/636; the PI catalog fetch + cache writes ride it in the background) and the port's daemon worker mirrors exactly that from its create path (worker/create.rs:531-544, fire-and-forget tokio::spawn of refresh_available_models, comment cites the TS boot behavior) - but the RPC in-process assembly (rpc/mod.rs run_rpc_mode) never spawns it. FROZEN SURFACES: untouched (one file, crates/pa-daemon/src/rpc/mod.rs, +17/-1; no wire/schema/prompt/session-JSONL/TUI bytes). The candidate's parity claim, oracle-verified: the SAME cache files, byte-identical payload+etag+fingerprint (modulo the embedded fetchedAt/refreshedAt timestamps which ARE the refresh times), same write-on-success conditions, same cadence (hour-gate catalog, 5-min-TTL private), only started at session boot - and the gam response payload is BYTE-IDENTICAL across arms (158239 bytes, sha256 908424519bf398dd61c3072991da2e225a5a1aa97aeb5e79f8d1de66f0f642e9 on all 8 ABBA blocks, both arms).

validity.notes: The ABBA's first-call class is network-fetch-dominated (the bench VM has internet: netcheck provider_catalog=200 @0.21s, pi_models=200 @0.19s); the write portion of the first call (~30-50ms on the ~50ms fresh-write regime) is a minority of the class, and the candidate changes NO write behavior (the same writes land at boot instead of on the first read; byte-oracle: identical payload+etag+fingerprint). The steady-state class carries the uniform ~50ms dispatch floor (the baseline record's separate candidate 2, mechanism-unprobed, not this lane's territory) - both arms pay it equally. gam-burst uses 16 calls in ONE process (the baseline battery's one-call-per-process design is exactly what misattributed the first-call class as a per-call cost). The response raw line includes the echoed request id (gam9=4 chars -> gam10=5 chars, the +1 byte at gam10 in every trial - driver artifact, not payload). The one-file patch is additive (a tokio::spawn of the same chain the daemon worker's create path already spawns); no moving-series file touched; no fold needed (the lane branched off the current tip and the tip did not move the touched file during the lane).
